english.title: Cause death by due care and fail to provide specimen
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), caused the death of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF DECEASED AND DATE OF DEATH IF DIFFERENT FROM DATE OF DRIVING..), by driving a mechanically propelled vehicle, being a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a

(A)_[road,]_
(B)_[public place,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD OR PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..), without

(C)_[due care and attention,]_
(D)_[reasonable consideration for other persons using the road,]_
(E)_[reasonable consideration for other persons using the place,]_

and, within 18 hours after that time, were required to provide

(F)_[a specimen or specimens of breath for analysis by means of a device of a type approved by the Secretary of State]_
(G)_[a specimen of blood for a laboratory test]_
(H)_[a specimen of urine for a laboratory test]_

pursuant to section 7 of the Road Traffic Act 1988, but, without reasonable excuse, failed to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3A(1)(c) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from the 28th June 2022 due to changes made by section 86 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022, which increased the penalty on indictment from 14 years imprisonment to life imprisonment. For the offence applying before the 28th June 2022, see H6003.
(ii) The minimum period of obligatory disqualification for this offence under section 34 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 was increased by section 86 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. See section 34(3), 34(3A) and 34(4ZA) which in some cases, increases the disqualification period to ten or five years.
(iii) Section 3A(1)(c) only applies in relation to a person driving a motor vehicle (not pedal cycles etc).
(iv) See section 24 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 for alternative verdicts.
(v) For the more usual offence wordings relating to the failure to provide specimens see H29 (drive/attempt to drive) and H30 (in charge).
(vi) When investigating offences of causing death/serious injury by careless/dangerous driving, including (if applicable) under influence of drink/drugs, then before preparing charges consideration must be given to the CPS charging standards/guidelines for these offences.
